title: A finite empirical segment has the actual joint-risk derivative
source_anchor: Samplinglib original mathematical supplement v1, 2026-10-20; units[1] and its complete formula proof
target_statement: Let P be a probability law on X×ℝ, with its actual input marginal Pₓ. Let K:W×X→ℝ be a scalar feature, and assume the actual response coordinate belongs to L²(P). Choose N>0 and two indexed parameter configurations w₀,w₁ of length N. Assume only their selected feature functions K(wₐʲ,·) belong to L²(Pₓ), for a=0,1 and every index j. Let ρ₀ and ρ₁ be their literal equally weighted Dirac empirical measures, retaining repeated indices. Define fρ(x)=∫K(w,x) dρ(w), F(ρ)=∫(fρ(x)−y)² dP(x,y), and V(w)=2∫(fρ₀(x)−y)K(w,x) dP(x,y). Every mixture (1−t)ρ₀+tρ₁ for 0≤t≤1 is a probability with integrable squared loss. V is integrable under both empirical laws, and the actual scalar risk along the mixture has right derivative ∫V dρ₁−∫V dρ₀ at zero.
